messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Incorrect joint policyholder name display",
 "problem_statement": "Joint policyholders receive letters displaying only one name or the wrong name due to incorrect system merging. This causes customer complaints and requires manual correction of outgoing correspondence.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "when there are joint policyholder names, the system merges them incorrectly—sometimes only showing one or the wrong one, and it’s causing real issues with policyholders.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-07T14:03:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’ve been having some trouble with joint policyholder names in outgoing letters.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-29T10:16:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "the system isn’t merging both names correctly — it’s only showing one joint policyholder names",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-03T12:32:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re seeing repeated issues where letters sent to joint policyholders only display one name — this leads to complaints and we need the joint policyholder names to appear correctly in all communications.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-29T15:23:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’ve got a few joint policyholder cases where the letters are coming out with mismatched names—causing complaints.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-07T14:03:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "The issue with letters merging multiple names on letters is causing us real problems — clients are complaining because only one name shows up, and sometimes it’s not even the right one.",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-29T13:22:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing real friction with clients.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-29T15:23:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when letters go out for policies with two named holders, the system only includes one name — and sometimes it’s the wrong one... led to some frustrated calls from policyholders and extra work for our team to fix the letters manually.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-29T10:16:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "our letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing confusion and we need this fixed.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-30T15:16:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Just need to know when we can expect the joint policyholder names to appear correctly in correspondence.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-29T15:23:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’ve got a repeat issue where letters sent to joint policyholders are only showing one name — it’s causing confusion and complaints from customers.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-03T12:32:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when we generate letters for policies with two named holders, the system only pulls through one name, sometimes the wrong one.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-29T10:16:00Z"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The claim is that Keelwater's system incorrectly merges joint policyholder names in outgoing letters, showing only one or the wrong name. Multiple quotes across sales, support, and account_management routes consistently describe the same product defect ('the system merges them incorrectly', 'the system only pulls through one name, sometimes the wrong one'), causing customer complaints and manual rework. This is a product behavior a squad could act on, not a pricing, contract, IT, or documentation issue, and no quote contradicts the pattern.", "verdict": "pass"}
